Our legacy choreographic architecture relied on asynchronous Kafka event chains, where distributed state transitions were scattered across multiple event handlers, making it difficult to track partial order failures or execute reliable compensations during third-party payment gateway timeouts. Production load tests across 40 worker node instances confirmed that Temporal sustained 18000 completed checkout workflows per minute, while eliminating distributed state divergence across 50 microservice boundaries.

Our legacy FileStore deployment wrote journal logs to the POSIX filesystem, which suffered from double write penalties where incoming write operations were committed twice, once to the journal file and once to the filesystem block allocation layer. Our legacy modulo hashing scheme mapped cache keys directly to server identifiers, which triggered massive cache invalidation cascades whenever a single cache node failed or when scaling cluster capacity, causing 90 percent of cache keys to be reshuffled and overwhelming backend databases with stampeding traffic.

The Architectural Decision Record approved a consistent hash ring assigning 256 virtual node tokens per physical server. When the cache cluster resizes, load simulation testing across 48 cache servers demonstrated that virtual node ring hashing maintained cache hit rates above 95 percent, while eliminating database traffic spikes during server failover events.

Our legacy deployment retained 18 months of metric data on local persistent disks, which caused frequent disk exhaustion and slow query execution times exceeding 45 seconds when aggregating historical metrics across 50000 time series.
